name: Codacy
basis: Codacy's own public pages and, for company basics only, the news sources named beside each fact
what: A cloud platform that runs code quality, security and coverage checks on repositories, with AI features that review pull requests and tools that feed its findings to coding agents.

facts.fact: Founded in 2012 by Jaime Jorge (CEO) and João Caxaria (CTO), headquartered in Lisbon.

facts.span: Founded in 2012 by developers Jaime Jorge and João Caxaria

facts.span: Codacy is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and GDPR compliant.

solutions.name: AI Reviewer
solutions.what: Opt-in pull request reviewer on GitHub that combines Codacy's static analysis with a language model, reads the PR, linked Jira or Linear tickets and repository instructions, and posts a review with a verdict, a summary, test suggestions and inline comments with suggested fixes. It can run automatically on the first review of a PR or on demand (button or public API).
solutions.status: generally available on GitHub for Team and Business plans; opt-in by an admin

solutions.name: Codacy Guardrails (AI Guardrails)
solutions.what: IDE extension plus the Codacy MCP server and Codacy CLI that give a user's own coding agent Codacy's scan results so the agent fixes issues; Codacy states it is not a language model itself.
solutions.status: available; free IDE extension, central configuration on paid plans

solutions.name: Codacy MCP Server
solutions.what: MCP server for the Codacy API (npm @codacy/codacy-mcp) exposing repositories, issues, security findings, pull requests and local analysis to MCP-compatible agents.

solutions.name: Auto-configure repository
solutions.what: Paid feature in which an AI coding agent reviews a repository and applies tool and code-pattern settings in Codacy, once per repository per day.

solutions.name: Codacy Skills
solutions.what: Skills for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI that drive the Codacy CLIs.

solutions.name: Smart False Positive Triage
solutions.what: AI triage that scores issues for likely false positives and surfaces them for manual review.

solutions.name: Codacy platform (Code Quality, Security, Coverage, AI Risk Hub, AI Inventory)
solutions.what: Static analysis, SAST/SCA/secrets/IaC/DAST, coverage gates and AI-usage inventory across repositories.

stories.span: Codacy's AI Reviewer is better aligned with its workflow

stories.what: Uses quality gates across 800 repositories and the IDE plugin with MCP integration; no AI Reviewer usage stated.

analysis: **The shape.** Codacy's AI Reviewer reads {sig:codacy-ai-reviewer} ({stage:codacy-ai-reviewer}). It is an opt-in reviewer for GitHub pull requests: it combines Codacy's static analysis with a language model, reads the pull request, a linked Jira or Linear ticket and the repository's instructions, and posts a review with a verdict, a summary, test suggestions and inline comments with suggested fixes. A person decides what to apply.

**Three levels hold with the reviewer on.** An admin turns the AI Reviewer on per repository or organisation, on GitHub, for Team and Business plans, so Reach 2 and Control 1 are marked available. Autonomy 1 rests on the Manually setting, in which a person starts each review with Run Reviewer or a call to the public API. Openness 2 holds as shipped: the docs give the reviewer's size limit (270,000 tokens or a 1 MB diff), list the context it sends to the model and what Codacy stores, and say secrets are redacted before sending.

**Where the evidence is strongest.** The documentation is specific. Teams write a review.md file whose template has a section for what the reviewer should ignore; people contest a comment by replying in the pull request; the reviewer posts through the Codacy GitHub App, whose permission table lists access scope by scope. A Codacy case study names BFI Finance, which compared the reviewer with its previous AI review tool and switched that tool off. Its figure of around 170 developers is the company's own, and a headcount, not a count of reviews.

**What would move it.** Autonomy 2: a page stating that the reviewer's suggested fixes are proposed actions a person approves one at a time. Reach 3: a published protocol or agent interface for the reviewer itself. Control 2: a page stating which high-impact actions need a person's approval. Openness 3: published test or evaluation results for the reviewer, with a method; an llms.txt and an OpenAPI description already resolve.

**Seen, and not counted.** The challenger lowered the reading of a posted review as an action: the reviewer changes no code, record or setting, so Autonomy rests on the manual mode. The Codacy MCP server and the review endpoint in the general REST API serve the whole platform, not the reviewer as an agent interface. The docs name OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock while another Codacy page says the reviewer runs on Gemini, so the models are not counted as listed. The SOC 2 Type 2 statement does not show that its scope covers the AI features.

article.title: AI Reviewer on the GAMMA-Ray Spectrum: {sig:codacy-ai-reviewer}
article.standfirst: The GAMMA-Ray studio reads Codacy's AI Reviewer from its public documentation: it reviews GitHub pull requests when an admin turns it on, a person applies what it suggests, and its data use and limits are written down.
body: Codacy, founded in 2012 by Jaime Jorge and João Caxaria and headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, runs code quality, security and coverage checks on repositories. Its AI Reviewer reviews pull requests on GitHub. A Codacy case study names BFI Finance, which switched off its previous AI review tool for it. We read it only from public sources, captured and hashed on 10 November 2026, and the published rules computed the card.

**Autonomy 1, Assists (available).** In the Manually setting a person starts each review, from the pull request or through the API. The reviewer posts a verdict, a summary and inline comments with suggested fixes; a person applies them.
**Reach 2, Integrated (available).** With the reviewer on, it combines GitHub pull request data, Codacy findings and a linked Jira or Linear ticket.
**Control 1, Stated (available).** Teams tell the reviewer what to ignore in a review.md file in the repository. A page on which high-impact actions need a person's approval would reach level 2.

**Openness 2, Documented.** The docs give the reviewer's size limit and the context it sends to the model, and say secrets are redacted. Published evaluation results with a method would reach level 3.
The card is beta and Codacy has not seen it. It can claim the card and add evidence; corrections are dated.

pt.title: O AI Reviewer da Codacy no GAMMA-Ray Spectrum: {sig:codacy-ai-reviewer}
pt.standfirst: O estúdio GAMMA-Ray lê o AI Reviewer da Codacy a partir da sua documentação pública: revê pull requests no GitHub quando um administrador o ativa, e uma pessoa aplica o que sugere.
body: A Codacy, fundada em 2012 por Jaime Jorge e João Caxaria e sediada em Lisboa, verifica a qualidade, a segurança e a cobertura do código em repositórios. O AI Reviewer revê pull requests no GitHub. Lemos apenas fontes públicas, capturadas e com hash a 10 de novembro de 2026.

**Autonomia 1 (opcional).** No modo manual, uma pessoa inicia cada revisão. **Alcance 2 (opcional).** Junta dados do pull request, resultados da Codacy e um ticket do Jira ou do Linear. **Controlo 1 (opcional).** A equipa diz ao revisor o que ignorar num ficheiro review.md.

**Abertura 2.** A documentação indica o limite de tamanho e os dados enviados ao modelo, e diz que os segredos são ocultados. O cartão é beta e a Codacy ainda não o viu; pode reclamá-lo e acrescentar evidência, e as correções são datadas.

method: A researcher-assessor gathered and captured the sources and mapped the evidence to indicators, without assigning a level. A challenger argued against every level three and four and every doubtful credit.
